status: FROZEN before tailC3000 was trained. The SHA-256 of this file is recorded in the commit that froze it. Amendments only before any result is seen.
title: Does Pavo's calibrated gain hold over the whole schedule?
origin: Pavo (variant C) beat the control arm after calibration at step 2000 on two independent training draws (evaluation/calibration_test_plan.json and evaluation/c2_replication_plan.json, -0.00154 and -0.00143 at 20 mm). Step 2000 is where screening stopped, two thirds of the 3 000-step cosine schedule. The control arm was run to step 3000 and has test-year forecasts. This plan runs Pavo's recipe to the end and scores it against that control.

models.tailC3000: bris/train/finetune_tail_c_full.yaml: finetune_tail_c with max_steps 3000, seed 20260909, step 3000
models.control3000: the control arm at step 3000, seed 20260909: ~/bris-models/control/control-step003000_inference.ckpt, test-year forecasts in ~/bris-runs/evaluation/control

test: exactly as evaluation/calibration_test_plan.json: 2025-08-01..2026-09-06, 4 members, BRIS_LEADTIMES=7, +30 h, strict common cases of both and MEPS, scripts/hits_and_calibration.py --cv month --replicates 5000 --meps --comparator control3000

primary_endpoint.measure: Brier score at 20 mm after month-out isotonic calibration, tailC3000 minus control3000
primary_endpoint.uncertainty: paired block bootstrap, seven-day blocks, 5000 replicates
primary_endpoint.positive_if: the upper 95 percent bound is below 0
primary_endpoint.negative_if: the lower 95 percent bound is above 0

secondary_reported: the same at 10 and 50 mm; raw Brier, ROC area, hits and false alarms
tailC3000 minus tailC2000 and control3000 minus control2000, calibrated, at 20 mm: what the last third of the schedule does to each recipe
not_claimed: A longer schedule on the same 18 months of data, one draw. Not more data; that needs new datasets.
